ai.definition: Indistinguishability Obfuscation (IO) is a theoretical cryptographic technique that transforms a program into an equivalent 'black box' version such that the original functionality remains intact, yet the internal logic and secrets are hidden from any observer.
ai.howItWorks: IO works by constructing functionally equivalent programs where it is computationally infeasible to distinguish between them. This is achieved using complex cryptographic techniques based on well-studied hardness assumptions, ensuring that while the program still functions as intended, its internal operations and secrets are obscured.
ai.problemSolved: IO addresses the challenge of protecting intellectual property and trade secrets within software without compromising functionality or usability.
ai.buildProcess: The build process involves complex cryptographic algorithms that transform a program into an obfuscated version. This is currently highly theoretical and not yet practical for widespread use.
ai.costDrivers: High computational resources, advanced mathematical expertise, and the need for rigorous security validation are key cost drivers.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Theoretical research with potential future applications in software protection and privacy-preserving technologies.
ai.regulation: Currently not regulated due to its theoretical nature. However, any practical implementation would require compliance with existing data protection regulations.
ai.risks: High risk of security breaches if the obfuscation is not robust enough or if underlying cryptographic assumptions are compromised.
ai.profitability: Not commercially viable at this stage but has potential for future applications in software licensing and intellectual property protection.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development could lead to practical implementations, particularly in areas where software protection and privacy are critical concerns.

glossary.def: A theoretical cryptographic technique that obfuscates the internal logic of a program while preserving its functionality.
Mathematical assumptions used in cryptography to ensure the security and robustness of cryptographic constructions.
Programs that perform the same task but have different internal logic, making it computationally infeasible to distinguish between them without knowledge of their secrets.

subsystems.name: Program representation
subsystems.role: turns the program to be hidden into a mathematical form the obfuscator can process.

subsystems.name: Hardness assumption layer
subsystems.role: provides the computational problem that makes the obfuscation secure.

subsystems.name: Randomized encoding
subsystems.role: hides intermediate values while preserving the final output of the program.

subsystems.name: Obfuscator and evaluator
subsystems.role: the two algorithms: one scrambles the program, the other runs the scrambled version.

subsystems.name: Security reduction
subsystems.role: proves that two functionally identical programs produce indistinguishable obfuscations.

buildSteps.title: Fix the program model
buildSteps.detail: Express the program to be obfuscated as a boolean circuit or branching program, so that it can be manipulated algebraically.

buildSteps.title: Choose a hardness assumption
buildSteps.detail: Base security on a computational problem believed to be hard, such as learning with errors or a multilinear map scheme.

buildSteps.title: Design a randomized encoding
buildSteps.detail: Encode each wire or step with secret randomness so that intermediate values are hidden but the final output is preserved.

buildSteps.title: Build the obfuscator
buildSteps.detail: Use the encoding to transform the program into an obfuscated program that evaluates correctly but reveals nothing about its internal logic.

buildSteps.title: Implement evaluation
buildSteps.detail: Write a procedure that takes the obfuscated program and an input, and computes the output without access to the original program.

buildSteps.title: Prove security
buildSteps.detail: Show that for any two functionally equivalent programs, the obfuscated versions are computationally indistinguishable to any efficient adversary.

buildSteps.title: Test on small examples
buildSteps.detail: Obfuscate simple functions, such as a few logic gates, to check that the scheme is correct and the security proof holds in practice.

buildSteps.title: Optimize for size and speed
buildSteps.detail: Reduce the enormous blow-up in program size and evaluation time, which currently makes even small programs impractical to obfuscate.

prerequisites.why: provides a well-studied hardness assumption on which modern candidate constructions are built.
early candidate obfuscators relied on them, but many were broken or proved too inefficient for real use.
the mathematical definition of indistinguishability obfuscation is well-established and guides construction.
current constructions blow up program size to impractically large levels, so only tiny programs could be handled.
recent constructions reduce to LWE plus other assumptions, but not yet to the most standard assumptions alone.

pathway.milestone: theoretical constructions exist with proofs under strong assumptions, but no practical implementation
pathway.unlocks: a clear mathematical definition and a target for future cryptographers.

pathway.milestone: simplify assumptions to well-studied ones and improve efficiency
pathway.unlocks: constructions that are easier to trust and closer to being implementable.

pathway.milestone: demonstrate obfuscation of small programs in practice
pathway.unlocks: proof that the approach works beyond theory and can handle real code fragments.

pathway.milestone: apply obfuscation to software protection and advanced cryptographic protocols
pathway.unlocks: practical tools for hiding secrets inside untrusted software.

pathway.milestone: if made practical, indistinguishability obfuscation could enable powerful cryptographic applications
pathway.unlocks: a foundation for secure computation and protection that is not achievable with today's cryptography.
